notes:
Passed with python3 -m mhs.driver check ... --backend fake. The evidence state is contract_checked, not an MHS-Device level, and this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware or upstream run was made. Install recon: README.md:12 names IsaacSim 4.5.0 and IsaacLab 2.2.0 and the card marks the package GPU, so the upstream environment cannot be installed or run under the no-network/no-hardware rules; no install command is recorded in the card. The fake backend is pure Python, needs only the SDK, and is written from the clone's own thruster, drag and reset equations. It was not compared with a real IsaacSim run; driver.py fidelity.gaps lists the differences (one 1/120 s fake step per env.step instead of the upstream decimation=2 substeps, one environment instead of four, no PhysX contacts or domain randomization, neutral buoyancy assumed, Python random.Random instead of torch/numpy generators, no rendering), and the fake's initial orientation/velocities are marked placeholders. The real observation is 17 values per environment (4 parallel environments in the clone's scene); the fake serves one environment and the same 17-value observation, so no array is omitted. Warnings in the passing report are expected of this family: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the next reset), G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x5 for action_space, dt, observation_space, reset and step, which come from the external DirectRLEnv base, and G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the integer/number inputs the bridge derives (ticks, action.values[*], seed twice). Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used; there are no catalogue requests. check-report.json is regenerated by the gate and is not part of the package.
